diveTitle: What actually happens when you unlock a PDF
diveSubtitle: Which restrictions can be removed, and which can't.
dive1Desc: There are two different things a PDF can restrict: an open password (you can't view the file without it) and permission restrictions (printing, copying, editing disabled even after opening). This tool removes the open password specifically — you must know it to unlock the file.
dive2Title: You need to know the password
dive2Desc: This isn't a password-cracking tool — you enter the existing password, and we remove it from the file so you don't have to enter it again each time. If you've genuinely forgotten a password, we can't recover or bypass it.
dive3Desc: A user password blocks opening the file entirely. An owner password allows opening but restricts actions like printing or copying, even without asking for a password upfront. Unlocking removes whichever password you provide, along with the restrictions tied to it.
dive4Title: What happens to the content itself
dive4Desc: Unlocking only changes the PDF's security settings — text, images, formatting, and page order are completely untouched. The output is visually and functionally identical to the original, just without the password requirement.
dive5Desc: If you need password protection again after unlocking — say, to change the password or remove specific restrictions while keeping others — use our Protect PDF tool afterward to add fresh security settings to the now-unlocked file.
dive6Title: When you're allowed to unlock a PDF
dive6Desc: This tool is meant for PDFs you own or have explicit permission to modify — your own password-protected documents, or files a client or colleague has given you the password for. Removing password protection without authorization can violate the owner's rights.
faqSubtitle: Quick answers on limits, privacy and results.
faq1Question: What types of PDF protection can you remove?
faq1Answer: We can remove owner-password restrictions (printing, editing, copying) automatically. For user-password protected PDFs (requiring a password to open), you'll need to enter the password — we cannot bypass unknown passwords.
faq2Question: Is it safe to upload my PDF?
faq2Answer: Yes. All files are transferred over HTTPS encryption and automatically deleted from our servers within 1 hour. We do not share your documents, and files are deleted after one hour.
faq3Question: What if I don't know the PDF password?
faq3Answer: If the PDF requires a password to open (user password) and you don't know it, we cannot unlock it. However, owner-password restrictions (which only limit editing/printing) are removed automatically without a password.
faq4Question: Will unlocking change the content of my PDF?
faq4Answer: No. Unlocking only removes the security restrictions — all text, images, formatting, and pages remain intact.
faq5Question: How many PDFs can I unlock at once?
faq5Answer: On the free plan you can upload and unlock up to 5 PDFs at once — Starter unlocks 10, Pro unlocks 20. Each file can be up to 10 MB on the free plan (100 MB on Starter and Pro). For larger batches, run multiple sessions.

guide.title: How to remove a password from a PDF
guide.intro: PDFs can have two kinds of password, and they are removed differently. Check which one your file has.

sections.title: Printing or copying is blocked (permissions password)
sections.text: If the PDF opens normally but won't let you print, copy or edit, it only has a permissions password. Upload it above and we remove those restrictions. You don't need to know the password.

sections.title: It asks for a password before opening (open password)
sections.text: If the PDF asks for a password just to open it, type that password once when you unlock it. We then save a copy without it, so it opens straight away from now on. We can't remove an open password you don't know: we don't guess or crack passwords.

sections.title: After unlocking
items: Set a new password with [Protect PDF](/protect-pdf).
Combine it with other files using [Merge PDF](/merge-pdf). Merging needs files that open without a password.

guide.footnote: Only unlock PDFs you own or have permission to change.
